skills.name: Swimming

source.section: Physical Skills — Swimming

notes: Surface swimming covers three times P.S. in yards/meters each melee round for P.E. minutes before fatigue. No attribute, S.D.C. or combat bonus is granted.
A failed roll leaves the swimmer afloat without covering distance. Three consecutive failed rolls cause submersion and drowning unless rescued.
Non-powered M.D.C. armor swimming requires staying afloat, depending on armor weight; no buoyancy formula is provided. Power armor swimming is permitted.

Surface swimming has the fatigue rate of running and is medium to heavy exertion, especially fast or long distances. Conditional storm and armor checks are shown separately; they do not automatically resolve simultaneous conditions or other armor movement penalties.

skills.name: Cardsharp
skills.description: Card tricks, deck manipulation, odds and card counting. Failed checks expose cheating. Cardsharp lists +4% from Palming; Palming lists +5% to Cardsharp. Use the larger overlapping bonus once (+5%), plus +6% from Gambling (Dirty Tricks).

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Computer Hacking
skills.description: Break computer access codes, trace data, bypass defenses and steal or sabotage data. Adds +5% once to Cryptography and Surveillance; Locksmith receives this bonus only for electronic/computer locks. Requires Literacy, Computer Operation, Computer Programming and at least Basic Mathematics.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Concealment
skills.description: Hide small items on the body, in the hands or on an unaware bystander. Items must be at most 14 inches long, 6 inches wide and 10 pounds. Small, light objects receive a situational +5%.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Find Contraband
skills.description: Locate illegal dealers and services; understand underworld practices, prices and penalties. Dealers typically pay only 20% of retail for contraband. Adds +10% to I.D. Undercover Agents.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Gambling (Standard)
skills.description: Understand games of chance, odds and winning strategies. Knows 1D4 games plus one per two I.Q. points (round up); game count is descriptive. Adds +5% to Basic Mathematics.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Gambling (Dirty Tricks)
skills.description: Cheat with marked cards, loaded dice, card counting and deck manipulation. Palming is required for hiding cards in the palm/sleeves and dealing from the bottom; it is not a prerequisite for the entire skill.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: I.D. Undercover Agents
skills.description: Recognize undercover law enforcement, spies, detectives, bounty hunters and other snoopers. Streetwise and Find Contraband each add +10% once.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Imitate Voices & Sounds
skills.description: Disguise voice, accent and regional speech; separately imitate wilderness calls and sounds (36% base). Copying a specific person requires familiarity/study and has a situational -20%. Adds +5% to Impersonation.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Palming
skills.description: Make a small object appear to vanish by concealing it in the hand. Adds +5% to Cardsharp, Concealment and Pick Pockets; Cardsharp also adds +4% to Palming.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Pick Locks
skills.description: Open key and tumbler locks using lock-picking tools. Does not cover sophisticated computer/electronic locks. Each attempt takes 1D6 melee rounds; a failed roll leaves the lock closed.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Pick Pockets
skills.description: Remove an item from an unaware person. Failure leaves the item in place and gives a 01-67% chance that the intended victim notices the attempt.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Prowl
skills.description: Move quietly and carefully using balance, positioning, low visibility and crawling. Failure reveals the character; successful stealth may permit a sneak attack. Listed in both Rogue and Physical; use one identity and the Rogue entitlement for these two classes.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Roadwise
skills.description: Know local streets, shortcuts, police posts, garages, hiding places and vehicle disposal locations in a named city/state or province. Typically reserved for car thieves, Operators and City Rats; other selections remain honor-system exceptions. Vehicle search times are descriptive.

source.section: Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.name: Safe-Cracking
skills.description: Study and open safes without harming their contents. Adds +5% to Pick Locks and Demolitions. Locksmith adds +4% and Mechanical Engineer +6% when learned. M.E. 14 or less imposes -10%. Explosive opening requires a separate Demolitions check.

Rogue Skills; cross-referenced skill descriptions

skills.description: Influence and distract through personal attraction. Adds +1% per M.A. point over 20 and per two P.B. points over 17 (round up). Adds +5% to Cardsharp, Sing and Dance. Pick Pockets, Palming and planting things gain +5% only against a seduced victim; intoxication/drugs give a situational +5%. Victim effects are descriptive.

skills.description: Diagnose, repair, wire and build complex electrical equipment. Requires Advanced Mathematics and Literacy. source.section: Electrical Skills

skills.name: Electricity Generation
skills.description: Use, link and repair solar, wind, hydro, battery, engine and generator systems; construction from scratch is outside this skill. Requires Basic Mathematics and at least Basic Electronics and Basic Mechanics. Alien or magical systems carry a -40% situational penalty.

source.section: Electrical Skills

skills.name: Robot Electronics
skills.description: Specialized micro-circuitry, military robotics, advanced computers, artificial intelligence, power armor and bionic electronics. Requires Electrical Engineer and Computer Programming. Alien or unfamiliar robot electronics carry a -40% situational penalty.

source.section: Electrical Skills

skills.name: Aircraft Mechanics
skills.description: Repair, rebuild and modify conventional aircraft, helicopters and hovercraft. Military aircraft work is limited to the body without Weapon Systems. Field repairs require suitable tools, materials and time; situational penalties vary from -5% to -40%, and extensive work requires a workshop.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Bioware Mechanics
skills.description: Identify, service and repair cybernetic and bionic machinery and electronics. This does not grant component design, biological Bio-System work or installation in a living body; installation requires Cyber-Doc training. Sophisticated or alien systems carry -20%. Requires Mechanical Engineer and Basic Mathematics. Field repairs require suitable tools, materials and time; situational penalties vary from -5% to -40%, and extensive work requires a workshop.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Locksmith
skills.description: Build, modify, repair and open mechanical or electronic locks. Requires Basic Electronics or Electrical Engineer. Electrical Engineer and Mechanical Engineer each add +5% once. Basic Electronics alone carries -10% for complex/high-tech locks; high-security systems may impose further situational penalties. Repeated failed electronic-lock attempts can damage the lock.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Mechanical Engineer
skills.description: Analyze, design, repair, build, modify or sabotage machinery. Make separate diagnostic, work and verification checks at the same proficiency. Requires Basic or Advanced Mathematics, Basic Electronics and Literacy; adds +5% once to Locksmith and Surveillance. Alien or unfamiliar machinery carries -30% and may remain beyond repair. Field repairs require suitable tools, materials and time; situational penalties vary from -5% to -40%, and extensive work requires a workshop.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Robot Mechanics
skills.description: Repair, modify, build or sabotage industrial robots, military drones, power armor and robot vehicles. Requires Mechanical Engineer, Electrical Engineer and at least Basic Mathematics. Alien, experimental, advanced military or magical robots carry a -30% situational penalty. Field repairs require suitable tools, materials and time; situational penalties vary from -5% to -40%, and extensive work requires a workshop.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Weapons Engineer
skills.description: Maintain, repair, modify and install military-class weapons and their vehicle systems; includes battery/E-Clip recharging and welding. Requires Mechanical Engineer. The +1 strike bonus applies only when using heavy or vehicular weapon systems and is descriptive here; alien or experimental systems carry -30%. Usually reserved for Operators and military specialists. Field repairs require suitable tools, materials and time; situational penalties vary from -5% to -40%, and extensive work requires a workshop.

source.section: Mechanical Skills

skills.name: Vehicle Armorer

source.section: Vehicle Armorer

skills.description: Modify vehicle bodies, armor and components with suitable facilities and parts. Automatically grants Basic Mechanics at +20%; adds +10% once to Automotive Mechanics. Armor, ram prows, speed tradeoffs, legal restrictions and construction activities remain descriptive.

source.section: Field Armorer & Munitions Expert

skills.name: Military Fortification

skills.description: Recall past navies, naval warfare and vessels, oceans and the beings who travel them.

skills.name: Naval Tactics

source.section: Naval Tactics

source.section: NBC Warfare (Nuclear, Biological, & Chemical)

skills.description: Understand precautions against nuclear, biological and chemical hazards and safe handling, cleanup and containment of hazardous materials.

skills.name: Parachuting

skills.description: Pack a chute, skydive and make precision landings, including HAHO, HALO and LALO insertion. Landing injury, opening complications and impact damage remain descriptive.

source.section: Recognize Weapon Quality

skills.description: Examine weapon durability, reliability, makers, wear, damage, modifications, copies, stolen identifiers and fair prices. Halve proficiency when the weapon is seen without physical examination.

skills.name: Trap & Mine Detection

source.section: Trap & Mine Detection

skills.description: Detect traps and mines visually, avoid them and disarm simple snares or trip wires. Mines, explosives and complex traps require Demolitions Disposal. skills.name: Jury-Rig

source.section: Jury-Rig

skills.description: Make temporary repairs or assemble scrap components. Requires at least Basic Mechanics and Basic Electronics; the respective Engineer skill also qualifies. Electrical Engineer, Mechanical Engineer or Field Armorer adds +10% once. Reliability lasts 4D6 hours or 2D4 days as appropriate; a second failed check leaves half functionality. Temporary reliability and activity outcomes remain descriptive.

source.section: Jury-Rig

skills.name: Boats: Ships/Seamanship

skills.name: Hover Craft (Ground)

source.section: Hover Craft (Ground)

skills.description: Pilot ground hover vehicles, including basic hovercycles and hover trucks. Jumps, tricks, gunfire dodging and stunt driving carry -20%; movement rates and distances remain descriptive.

skills.name: Hovercycles, Skycycles & Rocket Bikes

source.section: Hovercycles, Skycycles & Rocket Bikes

skills.description: Pilot specialized hovercycles, rocket bikes, skycycles and small jet-powered hover vehicles. Source stunts, jumps and dodges have no special skill penalty; distances and movement remain descriptive.

skills.name: Jet Aircraft

source.section: Jet Aircraft

skills.description: Pilot large and small commercial transport jets.

skills.name: Jet Packs

source.section: Jet Packs

skills.description: Pilot individual backpack flight units; normal flight capabilities and altitude remain descriptions.

skills.name: Jump Bike Combat (Juicer)

source.section: Jump Bike Combat (Juicer)

skills.description: Use the specialized Tarantula Jump Bike; reserved for Juicers, Crazies and similarly augmented people. Source attacks, auto-dodge and separate bike-jump attack check remain descriptive.

skills.name: Military: Combat Helicopters

source.section: Military: Combat Helicopters

skills.description: Pilot helicopters, including combat choppers, and operate their related weapon systems.

skills.name: Military: Jet Fighters

source.section: Military: Jet Fighters

skills.description: Fly, maneuver and use fighter jet weapons; aerial combat strategies remain descriptive.

skills.name: Military: Submersibles

source.section: Military: Submersibles

skills.description: Pilot underwater sleds, mini-subs and commercial or military submarines. Alien or unusual craft carry -20%; power armor and diving suits are separate.

skills.name: Military: Tanks & APCs

source.section: Military: Tanks & APCs

skills.description: Pilot heavy armored combat vehicles and other tracked vehicles.

skills.name: Military: Warships & Patrol Boats

source.section: Military: Warships & Patrol Boats

skills.description: Pilot warships, combat hydrofoils, patrol boats and amphibious transports; use their common equipment. Motor Boat or Ship skill can operate these craft at -12%; evasive and combat outcomes remain descriptive.

skills.name: Motorcycles & Snowmobiles

source.section: Motorcycles & Snowmobiles

skills.description: Pilot motorcycles, dirt bikes, mopeds, snowmobiles, jet sleds, miniature ATVs and similar small vehicles.

skills.name: Robots & Power Armor

source.section: Robots & Power Armor

skills.description: Pilot and operate robot vehicles and power armor without robot combat training bonuses. Weapon and combat feature use carries the source attack, strike, parry and dodge penalties unless Weapon Systems is acquired. Combat training, propulsion and underwater performance remain descriptions.

skills.name: Tracked & Construction Vehicles

source.section: Tracked & Construction Vehicles

skills.description: Pilot landcrawlers, half-tracks, light tanks, earthmovers and heavy construction vehicles. Tanks/APCs carry -15% and one fewer attack; conditional effects remain descriptive.

skills.name: Truck

source.section: Truck

skills.description: Drive large commercial cargo trucks and multi-ton transports.

skills.name: Water Scooters

source.section: Water Scooters

skills.description: Pilot small surface jet skis and underwater water sleds.

skills.name: Water Skiing & Surfing

source.section: Water Skiing & Surfing

skills.description: Use recreational skis, water boards, surfboards, sailboards and other wave-riding equipment.

skills.name: Navigation

source.section: Navigation

skills.description: Read maps, star charts and landmarks, compute courses and use instruments for land, air and water travel. Requires Basic Mathematics, Sensory Equipment and Literacy. Off-course distances and navigation outcomes remain descriptive.

skills.name: Weapon Systems

source.section: Weapon Systems

skills.description: Operate military vehicle, robot and power armor weapons, including turrets, missiles, lasers and rail guns. The +1 strike bonus applies to these systems rather than handheld weapons and remains descriptive.

skills.name: Rope Works

source.section: Rope Works

skills.description: Choose, tie, weave and make rope or cord, recognizing knots and tensile strengths. Failed knots are loose or unreliable; bound characters have -10% to escape or slip the knots. Conditional outcomes remain descriptive.

skills.name: Boat Building

source.section: Boat Building

skills.description: Build rafts, rowboats, canoes and small flatbed boats; failed construction leaks. Construction times and patching remain descriptions.

skills.name: Carpentry

source.section: Carpentry

skills.description: Prepare, preserve, cut and work wood; recognize craftsmanship and construct or repair wooden objects. Adds 10% to Boat Building and 5% to Trap Construction.

skills.name: Dowsing

source.section: Dowsing

skills.description: Locate fresh water by nature knowledge and deductive analysis; source requires two consecutive successful checks to locate it.

skills.name: Fasting

source.section: Fasting

skills.description: Endure extended periods without food or water; weakening, temporary attribute loss and recovery remain source descriptions.

skills.name: Identify Plants & Fruit

source.section: Identify Plants & Fruit

skills.description: Identify wild vegetation, edible foods, herbs and medicinal plants while avoiding poisonous varieties. Searching time remains descriptive.

skills.name: Land Navigation

source.section: Land Navigation

skills.description: Stay on course by landmarks, distance estimates, trail marking and observation. Does not require Literacy or Mathematics; symbolic map reading carries 20% penalty. Travel and drift remain descriptions.

skills.name: Preserve Food

source.section: Preserve Food

skills.description: Prepare foods for storage by canning, drying, smoking, salting or pickling.

skills.name: Skin & Prepare Animal Hides

source.section: Skin & Prepare Animal Hides

skills.description: Skin, tan, stretch and preserve animal hides as fur or leather; adds 5% to Sewing and Leather Working.

skills.name: Spelunking

source.section: Spelunking

skills.description: Explore and navigate cave systems, recognize equipment, rock formations and cave dangers. Climbing adds 5% to this skill.

skills.name: Track & Trap Animals

skills.description: Recognize and follow animal tracks and habits; trapping uses its separate normal percentage. Tracking humans and disarming traps intended for humans use half the relevant proficiency.

skills.name: Wilderness Survival

source.section: Wilderness Survival

skills.description: Find water, food, shelter and help when stranded in forests, deserts or mountains. Also listed in Espionage; retain one acquired skill identity.

skills.name: Detect Ambush

source.section: Detect Ambush

skills.description: Recognize terrain and locations suitable for ambush; this does not identify individual prowling enemies.

skills.name: Detect Concealment

source.section: Detect Concealment

skills.description: Spot deliberately concealed structures, camouflage, traps, doors or compartments; construct unobtrusive shelters. Adds 5% to Camouflage; ordinary observation uses Perception.

skills.name: Disguise

source.section: Disguise

skills.description: Alter appearance using makeup, wigs, dyes and other effects; adds 5% to Impersonation and Undercover Ops.

skills.name: Escape Artist

source.section: Escape Artist

skills.description: Escape restraints using flexible joints, knot knowledge, positioning and concealed tools. Pick Locks is separate; this training adds 5% to it.

skills.name: Forgery

source.section: Forgery

skills.description: Copy documents, signatures and identity papers from an original or photocopy. Recognizing counterfeits carries 10% penalty; Art adds 10% to normal proficiency.

skills.name: Impersonation

source.section: Impersonation

skills.description: Impersonate a type of person or a specific individual using knowledge, dress, protocol and language; specific individuals use the separate normal percentage. Adds 10% to Undercover Ops. Encounters and discovery remain descriptive.

skills.name: Intelligence

source.section: Intelligence

skills.description: Recognize and analyze enemy information, troops, operations and evidence; estimate ranges, threats and strategic importance. Failed evidence remains inconclusive or misinterpreted.

skills.name: Interrogation

source.section: Interrogation

skills.description: Question unwilling informants and assess deception using interview tactics. Source restrictions and 20% penalty for supernatural beings remain descriptions.

skills.name: Tracking (humans & robots)

source.section: Tracking (humans & robots)

skills.description: Identify and follow humanoid or robot tracks and conceal one's own trail using the same normal proficiency. Tracking animals or supernatural beings uses half proficiency; distraction and countertracking penalties remain descriptive.

skills.name: Undercover Ops

source.section: Undercover Ops

skills.description: Blend into groups and assume false identities to gather information or evidence. Usually reserved for investigative, espionage or criminal occupations; eligibility remains table guidance.

skills.name: Appraise Goods
skills.description: Assess ordinary goods and their wholesale/retail value. Two selections grant 15% and one excluded goods category; retain that category as the specialty.

source.section: Appraise Goods

skills.name: Begging
skills.description: Solicit food, money or clothing. Disguise receives 5% only when posing as a beggar or refugee; local legal and encounter outcomes remain descriptive.

source.section: Begging

skills.name: Breed Dogs
skills.description: Raise, mate, tame and train domestic or wild canines. The separate normal check trains tricks and specific work; trained animals are not familiars.

source.section: Breed Dogs

skills.name: Cybernetics: Basic
skills.description: Understand ordinary cybernetic implants and make minor adjustments before implantation. Cannot perform surgery, implant or remove cybernetics, or repair military bionics.

source.section: Cybernetics: Basic

skills.name: Excavation
skills.description: Excavate relics, tunnels and underground chambers safely; assess depth, soil and structural support. Adds 5% Spelunking and 5% Dowsing only for underground water.

source.section: Excavation

skills.name: Gemology
skills.description: Identify and appraise precious stones/metals. Recognizing fakes has a 10% penalty. Adds 5% Mining/Prospecting.

source.section: Gemology

skills.name: General Repair & Maintenance
skills.description: Maintain simple mechanisms and household gear. Diagnosis and actual repair use the same normal proficiency. Complex, high-tech, alien or very damaged items use half proficiency; retries and repaired damage remain descriptive.

source.section: General Repair & Maintenance

skills.name: Lore: American Indians
skills.description: Know Native American tribes, traditions, history, weapons, gods and spirits. The descent-specific check applies only to characters of Native American descent.

source.section: Lore: American Indians

skills.name: Lore: Cattle & Animals
skills.description: Know livestock and wild animal habits, predators, defense, uses and associated tales of spirits or animal magic.

source.section: Lore: Cattle & Animals

skills.name: Lore: D-Bee
skills.description: Know mortal alien humanoids and their culture in the retained region. A smaller geographic region uses the separate 10% bonus check; choose the applicable regional scope at the table.

source.section: Lore: D-Bee

skills.name: Lore: Demons & Monsters
skills.description: Know supernatural monsters, demons, powers, weaknesses and folklore of the retained geographic region. Different regions count as separate skill selections.

source.section: Lore: Demons & Monsters

skills.name: Lore: Faeries & Creatures of Magic
skills.description: Know Faerie Folk, dragons and other long-lived magical creatures, their myths, habits and abilities.

source.section: Lore: Faeries & Creatures of Magic

skills.name: Lore: Juicer
skills.description: Know Juicer culture, variants, abilities, drugs, side effects, gangs and notable figures.

source.section: Lore: Juicer

skills.name: Lore: Magic
skills.description: Know magical theories, history and practitioners without acquiring magic powers or Techno-Wizard use. Separate normal checks recognize symbols/circles and enchantment. Artifact information depends on the item; unknown or alien artifacts carry a 15% penalty.

source.section: Lore: Magic

additional_checks.name: Recognize magic symbols, runes and circles

skills.name: Lore: Psychics & Psionics
skills.description: Know psionic powers, psychic beings, psychic weapons and related myths without becoming psychic.

source.section: Lore: Psychics & Psionics

skills.name: Mining / Prospecting
skills.description: Prospect, pan, identify minerals and operate mining/refining equipment. Prospecting is the source cross-reference to this same skill. Mining explosives use Demolitions at a 20% penalty; specific operations remain descriptive.

source.section: Mining / Prospecting

skills.name: Mythology
skills.description: Know famous world myths and the retained culture's folklore. Adds 5% Lore: Magic and Lore: Demons & Monsters.

source.section: Mythology

skills.name: Salvage
skills.description: Find, identify, recover and evaluate wreckage, junk and spare parts. Rebuilding requires time, parts and the applicable skills.

source.section: Salvage

skills.name: Whittling & Sculpting
skills.description: Carve wood, bone and horn into figures or simple objects. One selection is amateur; two confer professional quality and 10% once.

source.section: Whittling & Sculpting

skills.name: Horsemanship: General
skills.description: General riding, care, breed assessment, breeding and wagon handling. The second normal check handles jumps, tricks, racing and control. While mounted: +1 parry/dodge, +1D4 melee damage, and charge +1D6/two actions. These contextual effects are not added to standing combat totals.

source.section: Horsemanship: General

skills.name: Horsemanship: Exotic Animals
skills.description: Ride and care for tame exotic mounts. Wild untamed creatures require exceptional powers; unfamiliar ground mounts -12%, flying/climbing mounts -20%, unfamiliar Earth horses -10% on the second check remain situational descriptions.

source.section: Horsemanship: Exotic Animals

skills.name: Horsemanship: Cowboy
skills.description: Specialized Cowboy riding; not available to most occupations. While mounted: +1 initiative at levels 2/5/10/15, fall/impact+2, parry+2, dodge/entangle/ensnare+2, melee damage+1D4, charge+2D6 S.D.C./+1D6 M.D., horse strike+4 apply only while mounted; these contextual effects are not added to standing combat totals.

source.section: Horsemanship: Cowboy

skills.name: Horsemanship: Cossack
skills.description: Exclusive to the Cossack occupation in World Book 17. While mounted: +1 initiative at levels 1/4/8/12/15, fall/impact+2, parry/dodge+2, melee damage+6, charge+2D6 S.D.C./+1D6 M.D., horse strike+3 apply only while mounted; these contextual effects are not added to standing combat totals.

source.section: Horsemanship: Cossack

skills.name: Horsemanship: Cyber-Knight
skills.description: Exclusive Cyber-Knight training. While mounted: +1 initiative at levels 1/5/9/14, fall/impact+2, parry/dodge+2, melee damage+6, charge+3D6 S.D.C./+2D6 M.D., horse strike+2 apply only while mounted; these contextual effects are not added to standing combat totals.

source.section: Horsemanship: Cyber-Knight

skills.name: Horsemanship: Skilled Equestrians or Knight
skills.description: Skilled equestrian or non-Cyber-Knight training, available only through source occupation permission. While mounted: +1 initiative, fall/impact+1, parry/dodge+2, melee damage+1D6, charge+2D6 S.D.C./+1D6 M.D., horse strike+1 apply only while mounted; these contextual effects are not added to standing combat totals.

source.section: Horsemanship: Skilled Equestrians or Knight

skills.name: Branding
skills.description: Tether, control and mark animals; recognize common insignias and emblems.

source.section: Branding

skills.name: Breaking/Taming a Wild Horse
skills.description: Acclimatize and tame a wild horse. Exotic/alien animals carry 10% penalty; wild bulls/broncos and steer wrestling 15%. Time, contests and outcomes remain descriptions.

source.section: Breaking/Taming a Wild Horse

skills.name: Herding Cattle
skills.description: Lead, direct, calm, care for and control livestock; recognize illness, gather strays and mend fences.

source.section: Herding Cattle

skills.name: Roping
skills.description: Use a lariat to snare, tether, lead and control animals. Cowboys/Saddle Tramps receive another 10% beyond occupational training. Entangle gains at 1/3/5/7/9/11/14 and combat maneuvers remain sourced descriptions; no unconditional combat or class bonus granted to ordinary paths.

source.section: Roping

skills.name: Climbing

source.section: Climbing

skills.description: Climb sheer surfaces with appropriate tools and techniques; rappelling includes ascending and descending with ropes. Roll every 20 feet; two consecutive failures cause a fall.

skills.name: Aerobic Athletics

source.section: Aerobic Athletics

skills.description: The percentage measures sense of balance. Aerobic exercise develops grace and basic self-defense; +2 kicking damage applies to kicks only.

skills.name: Juggling

source.section: Juggling

skills.description: Keep small objects in the air through coordinated hand movements; also develops hand-eye coordination.

skills.name: S.C.U.B.A.

source.section: S.C.U.B.A.

skills.description: Use underwater breathing equipment and skin-diving techniques. Swimming is required. Safe depth is about 120 feet without decompression or special equipment; swimming pace and fatigue depend on the situation.

skills.name: Forced March

source.section: Forced March

skills.description: March with a field pack and weapons at a coordinated pace. Forced-march endurance is five times normal; speed is roughly 60% of Speed, with a minimum of 8. These travel effects apply to forced marches only.

skills.name: Outdoorsmanship

source.section: Outdoorsmanship

skills.description: Experience living off the land hardens the character for outdoor life. Requires Wilderness Survival; adds +5 to Dowsing, Fasting, Identify Plants and Fruit, and Wilderness Survival.

skills.name: Wrestling

source.section: Wrestling

skills.description: Sport wrestling adds body block/tackle, pin/incapacitate on natural 18-20, and crush/squeeze. Normal tackle/squeeze damage is 1D4 S.D.C.; size can increase it. A pin holds both participants until released.

skills.name: Kick Boxing

source.section: Kick Boxing

skills.description: Supplementary fighting training adds Roundhouse Kick 3D6, Axe Kick 2D8, Knee Strike 1D8 and Leap Kick 3D8 (two actions). Ordinary mortals inflict S.D.C.; supernatural and robotic strength change damage type or dice according to the source.

skills.name: Fencing

source.section: Fencing

skills.description: Requires W.P. Sword; W.P. Knife is optional. While using a sword or dagger: +1 strike and parry. Sword damage gains +1D6. These weapon-specific bonuses are not added to standing hand-to-hand totals.

source.section: Fencing

skills.name: Acrobatics

source.section: Acrobatics

skills.description: Primary percentage measures sense of balance. Automatic kick at first level does 1D8 S.D.C. damage. Basic climb and prowl have no level growth; they yield to the separately learned full skill, which receives the source bonus instead. No fear of heights.

source.section: Acrobatics

skills.name: Gymnastics

source.section: Gymnastics

skills.description: Primary percentage measures sense of balance. Automatic kick at first level does 2D4 S.D.C. damage. Basic climb and prowl have no level growth; they yield to the separately learned full skill, which receives the source bonus instead.

source.section: Gymnastics

skills.name: Hunting

source.section: Hunting

skills.description: Hunt and prepare animals for food; understand habits, baiting, trapping, blinds and tree stands. Adds +2 to Prowl, +5 to Track & Trap Animals, +5 to Skin & Prepare Animal Hides, +4 to Imitate Voices & Sounds, and +10 to Cook game animals only.

skills.name: Sniper

source.section: Sniper

skills.description: Long-range marksmanship with single-shot weapons. Adds +2 to strike on Called or Aimed Shots only; does not apply to automatic burst fire. Eligible weapons include bows, crossbows, bolt-action rifles and energy rifles switched to single shots. This conditional bonus is not a standing hand-to-hand strike bonus.

skills.name: Brewing: Basic

source.section: Brewing: Basic

skills.description: Prepare fermented grain/fruit drinks and common nonalcoholic beverages. The first percentage measures success; the second measures quality, with a lower roll giving a tastier drink. Strong spirits, champagne and fine wines are excluded. Adds +5 to Holistic Medicine if known.

skills.name: Wardrobe & Grooming

source.section: Wardrobe & Grooming

skills.description: Clothing, make-up, hair, perfume, bearing, fashion and presentation. Adds +2 to Disguise, Impersonation, Performance, Undercover Ops and Seduction. P.B. gains +1 only when dressed to impress; this situational contribution is not added to the saved standing attribute.
